claim_formal: ∃c>0 ∀ a1,a2≥1,b1,b2≥0 with a1b2≠a2b1 ∃C ∀X≥3: |Σ_{n≤X} λ(a1n+b1)λ(a2n+b2)| ≤ C·X/(log X)^c

quote_A.text: There is an absolute constant c>0 such that, for every fixed choice of integers ... ≤ C X/(log X)^c

quote_B.text: We prove the ordinary two-point Chowla conjecture.

notes: Second headline: binary corrected Elliott conjecture for ordinary averages (qualitative, ∀f1,f2 nonpretentious: average → 0), also in Lean. 'Implied constants need not be effective.' Prefix ∃c∀forms (C, X are bound constants).

claim_formal: ∀ p, ∀ finite k/ℚp, ∀ smooth proper geom. connected curve X/k of genus ≥2: X(k) → {sections of π1(X)→G_k}/conj is bijective

quote_A.text: the map X(k) → {s: G_k → π1(X) ... }/π1(X_{\bar k}) is bijective

quote_B.text: We prove the local p-adic section conjecture for smooth proper geometrically connected curves of genus at least two

notes: Matrix: bijection between rational points and section classes; M7 (identification of named sets) vs M1/M5. Global section conjecture for X0(N), X1(N) follows using established finite-descent theorems (corollary).

claim_formal: ∀ number fields F1,F2, ∀ solvably closed Galois E_i/F_i, ∀ continuous open α: Gal(E1/F1)→Gal(E2/F2): ∃! field embedding j: E2↪E1 inducing α

quote_A.text: Every continuous open homomorphism ... is induced by a unique field embedding j: E_2 ↪ E_1.

quote_B.text: We prove Uchida's conjecture on open homomorphisms of Galois groups.

notes: Uniqueness was already proved by Uchida; existence ends via Hoshi's cyclotomic criterion (prior result), hence the flag.

claim_formal: ∀ curve C of genus ≥2, ∀ composite n≥4, ∀ d coprime to n, ∀ L∈Pic^d(C), ∀ m,k: P_k H^m(X^B) = W_{2k} H^m(X^B) = W_{2k+1} H^m(X^B)

quote_A.text: P_kH^m(X^B,Q)=W_{2k}H^m(X^B,Q)=W_{2k+1}H^m(X^B,Q) for all m,k≥0

quote_B.text: Together with the established prime-rank cases, this gives the equality in every coprime rank.

notes: Paper itself covers composite rank only; full fixed-determinant P=W follows only with prior prime-rank theorem (Maulik–Shen). Alternative: O5 for the composite-rank part alone.

claim_formal: ∀ generalized lc pair (X0,B0+M) on a globally Weil ℚ-factorial compact Kähler fourfold with rational boundary, ∀ sequence of projective small flip diagrams with prescribed ample signs: the sequence is finite

quote_A.text: Every sequence of generalized log canonical flips on a normal irreducible globally Weil ℚ-factorial compact Kähler fourfold terminates

quote_B.text: We prove the projective four-dimensional case of the Termination of Flips Conjecture for ordinary log canonical pairs with rational boundary

notes: Termination = no infinite flip sequence; could be read as M4. Restricted to dimension 4, rational boundary, projective small diagrams (Hacon–Xie Conj. 1.15 in a 4-dim rational form). Also bundles projective lc fourfold MMP termination and Kähler klt MMP termination.

claim_formal: ∀ connected simple complex G, ∀ smooth projective connected curve X, ∀ c∈ℂ∖ℚ: D_c(Bun_G(X)) ≃ D_{-1/(rc)}(Bun_{G^∨}(X))

quote_A.text: For every c∈ℂ∖ℚ there is an equivalence of presentable ℂ-linear DG categories D_c(Bun_G(X)) ≃ D_{-1/(rc)}(Bun_{G^∨}(X))

quote_B.text: Theorem gives its unramified de Rham equivalence in the irrational range.

notes: Quantum geometric Langlands conjecture (Stoyanovsky/Gaitsgory; Bogdanova Conj. 1) settled for irrational levels, unramified, de Rham. If the conjecture is regarded as posed only at irrational level, O1.

quote_A.text: For every real r>2 there is a finite constant C_r such that ‖V_r(F,G)‖_{L^{3/2}} ≤ C_r‖F‖_3‖G‖_3

quote_B.text: this proves the symmetric scalar estimate in Thiele's Problem~13

notes: Boundedness estimate; M8 vs M1 ambiguous. Lean formalizes only the maximal (single-increment) estimate ∃C∀F,G, a special case of the variation bound. Also a dyadic absolute-sum bound with explicit constant 40.

quote_A.text: d_p(n,D) ≤ exp(C_{p,D}(log n)^{γ(p)})

quote_B.text: answering Naor's sublinear-dimension question for p ≠ 2

notes: Also exact embeddings need Θ(n^2) dimension (M9-type side result) and a log n lower bound. Upper exponent not claimed optimal.

claim_formal: ∀ δ∈(0,1/3): ∃ poly-time reduction 3SAT→graphs with SAT ⇒ 3-colorable and UNSAT ⇒ α(G)<δ|V| (NP-hard to distinguish)

quote_A.text: for every fixed 0<δ<1/3, it is NP-hard to distinguish three-colorable graphs from graphs in which every independent set has fewer than δ times the number of vertices

quote_B.text: Combining it with the preceding reductions resolves the constant-palette conjecture ... Theorem combines this stronger form of soundness with three-colorability

notes: The summary's lead statement (NP-hard to c-color 3-colorable graphs) was already obtained via Fei–Minzer–Wang + earlier reductions per the paper ('recovers the constant-palette hardness theorem'); the new main theorem strengthens soundness to small independence ratio. If headline taken as the c-coloring corollary, rule 9 gives O9.

claim_formal: ∀ c≥0 ∃ bin-packing instance I (items >1/6) ∃ B: LP(I)=B ∧ OPT(I)>B+c

quote_A.text: For every integer c≥0, there is a finite rational bin-packing instance I and an integer B such that ... LP(I)=B, OPT(I)>B+c

quote_B.text: We disprove the Modified Integer Round-Up Conjecture for bin packing

notes: Also NP-hardness of constant-additive approximation (answers Williamson–Shmoys Ch.17 Problem 3, P3, negatively; additive algorithm exists iff P=NP). Lean main_results bundles both.

claim_formal: ∀ n≥4, ∀ graphical degree vector d: t_mix(lazy switch chain on Ω_d) ≤ 2n^8

quote_A.text: For every n≥4 and every graphical degree vector d, t_mix(d) ≤ 2n^8.

quote_B.text: We prove the simple-undirected form of the Kannan–Tetali–Vempala conjecture

notes: KTV conjecture (Unified22 Conj 1.1) is posed jointly for bipartite, directed, and simple-undirected models; this settles the simple-undirected model (bipartite by FQW). By rule 6 O5; O1 if the simple-undirected formulation counts as its own problem. Corollary: exact uniform sampler.

claim_formal: ∀ d≥1 ∃ B(d)<∞ ∀ real planar polynomial vector field V of degree ≤d: #limit cycles(V) ≤ B(d)

quote_A.text: For each integer d≥1, there is a finite nonnegative integer B(d) such that every real planar polynomial vector field of degree at most d has at most B(d) limit cycles

quote_B.text: This establishes the uniform boundedness assertion in the second part of Hilbert's sixteenth problem.

notes: Hilbert 16 (part 2) asks for the maximum number; finiteness of H(d) settles only the existential part (non-effective). Could be O1 if the uniform-boundedness question counts as the posed problem. Lean covers only the quintic Liénard result (exact max 2, Lins Neto–de Melo–Pugh degree 5 case).

claim_formal: ∃ finite T⊂ℤ^3: T tiles ℤ^3 by translations ∧ ∀ tiling A⊕T=ℤ^3: A not fully periodic (and same for T+[0,1]^3 in ℝ^3)

quote_A.text: There is a finite nonempty set T⊂ℤ^3 such that T tiles ℤ^3 by translations, but no translation set A ... is invariant under a subgroup of finite index

quote_B.text: This gives a negative resolution of the periodic tiling conjecture in dimension three.

notes: Conjecture already refuted in high dimension (Greenfeld–Tao); this settles d=3, the least possible. Lean adds minimality (IsLeast d=3) using prior planar results.

claim_formal: ∀ Coxeter systems (W,S),(W',S'), ∀ u≤b, u'≤b', ∀ poset iso ι:[u,b]→[u',b']: P_{u,b}=P'_{u',b'}

quote_A.text: If ι:[u,b]→[u',b'] is an isomorphism of abstract Bruhat interval posets, then P^W_{u,b}(q)=P^{W'}_{u',b'}(q).

quote_B.text: This resolves the full combinatorial invariance conjecture positively.

claim_formal: ∀ finite simple cubic bipartite planar 3-connected graph G ∃ Hamiltonian cycle in G

quote_A.text: Every finite simple undirected graph that is cubic, bipartite, planar, and 3-vertex-connected has a Hamiltonian cycle.

quote_B.text: We prove Barnette's conjecture

notes: Corollaries: edge avoidance; Pfaffian 3-edge-path version via GSW equivalence.

claim_formal: ∀ C>0 ∃ n ∃ Boolean f:{-1,1}^n→{-1,1} nonconstant: Σ_i f̂({i}) > C√deg(f)

quote_A.text: For every real C>0, there are a positive integer n and a nonconstant Boolean function f ... such that Σ f̂({i}) > C√deg(f)

quote_B.text: We disprove the Gopalan–Servedio square-root conjecture, even up to an arbitrary constant factor.

notes: Also recorded in O'Donnell's problem list (P3 arguable); treated as named conjecture.

claim_formal: ∀ n≥2, ∀ dominant λ,μ,ν of Spin(2n) with λ+μ+ν∈Q, ∀ N≥1: (V(Nλ)⊗V(Nμ)⊗V(Nν))^G≠0 → (V(λ)⊗V(μ)⊗V(ν))^G≠0

quote_A.text: for every positive integer N, (V(λ)⊗V(μ)⊗V(ν))^G≠0 ⟺ (V(Nλ)⊗V(Nμ)⊗V(Nν))^G≠0

quote_B.text: Kapovich and Millson formulated the analogous root-lattice assertion for simply laced groups. We prove its type-D case.

notes: Stated as ⇔ but the forward direction is trivial; content is the implication (M1; M5 arguable). Type D of the simply-laced saturation conjecture; type E remains.

claim_formal: C_{β_c}(r) = B·r^{-1/4}(log r)^{1/8}(1+o(1)) as r→∞ for the nearest-neighbor square-lattice XY model at β_c, some B∈(0,∞)

quote_A.text: There is a constant B_XY∈(0,∞) such that C_{b_c}(r)=B_XY r^{-1/4}(log r)^{1/8}(1+o(1))

quote_B.text: Janke records the critical prediction ... |x|^{-1/4}(log|x|)^{1/8}; Theorem establishes the leading equivalent

notes: Posed object is a physics (Kosterlitz RG/BKT) prediction rather than a named math conjecture; P1 used for 'predicted answer'. Family also proves BKT essential singularity √(βc−β)log ξ→A, exponent −1/4, height universality; center-magnetization and spin-field results are conditional on stated inputs.

claim_formal: ∃ stable radial pair potential φ on ℝ^3 (bounded continuous, |φ(r)|≤Cr^{-3-1/32}) ∃ open density interval I ∃ β_c ∀ ρ∈I: D^-_β f(β_c,ρ) > D^+_β f(β_c,ρ)

quote_A.text: There is a bounded continuous function φ ... and a common inverse temperature β_c ... f'_-(β_c,ρ)>f'_+(β_c,ρ)

quote_B.text: realizing the type of transition sought in Simon's continuum problem

notes: Simon's 1984 problem list (numbered) treated as P3. First manuscript explicitly declines to claim the problem (only φ=o(r^{-3})); the bounded algebraic-decay version is the one matching it; whether Simon's problem demands more (e.g. Lennard-Jones-type, phase identification) is unclear, so O1 is low-confidence.

claim_formal: ∀ infinite cardinal λ ∃ μ(λ) ∀ AEC K with LS(K)≤λ: (∃κ≥μ(λ) K categorical in κ) → (∀κ'≥μ(λ) K categorical in κ')

quote_A.text: For every infinite cardinal λ there is a cardinal μ(λ)≥λ such that ... for every AEC K with LS(K)≤λ

quote_B.text: Proves Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture in ZFC

notes: Lean formalizes only the CH obstruction (under CH an AEC categorical on a tail but not at the Hanf bound ℶ_{ω2}), showing the prescribed-threshold form is not ZFC-provable (an O4-type secondary result).

claim_formal: ∃ group G: G torsion-free ∧ word-hyperbolic ∧ ¬residually finite

quote_A.text: There exists a torsion-free word-hyperbolic group that is not residually finite.

quote_B.text: answering the residual-finiteness question for hyperbolic groups negatively

notes: Corollary: G not linear over any field; via Kapovich–Wise some hyperbolic group is not virtually torsion-free.

claim_formal: ∀ M>0, 0<|a|<M ∃ ε>0, ∀ᵍ (residual/comeagre) vacuum data d∈U_ε near Kerr bridge: MGHD(d) has no future C^0∩W^{1,2}_loc extension

quote_A.text: the set of d∈U_ε for which the full development admits a future extension ... is meagre in U_ε

quote_B.text: Proves local strong cosmic censorship near each fixed rotating subextremal Kerr bridge.

notes: Generic = Baire-residual. Local (near Kerr) form of strong cosmic censorship; companion manuscripts give C^1 and C^2 versions.

quote_A.text: χ(A^{⊗n}) = nχ(A) = (n/ln2) max_{0≤p≤1}{...}. In particular, C(A_{γ,ν})=χ(A_{γ,ν})

quote_B.text: Leditzky, Kaur, Datta, and Wilde identified its unrestricted classical capacity as an open problem

notes: Open-problem citation is for ordinary amplitude damping; generalized channel is the stated target. Corollary: additivity with any finite-dimensional partner channel (not in Lean).

claim_formal: ∀ unital C*-algebra A, ∀ Hilbert space H, ∀ bounded unital homomorphism π:A→B(H) ∃ invertible S: S π(·) S^{-1} is a *-homomorphism

quote_A.text: There exists an operator S∈B(H), invertible with bounded inverse, such that ρ(a)=Sπ(a)S^{-1} is a *-homomorphism.

quote_B.text: This resolves Kadison's similarity conjecture positively.

notes: Corollary: universal hyperreflexivity constant for all von Neumann algebras (also an old open question). Lean includes similarityTheorem plus the uniform commutator estimate.

claim_formal: ∀ ε∈(0,1), ∀ MASA A⊆M⊆B(H), ∀ x=x*∈M: x is (ε, r_ε)-so-pavable over A with r_ε ≤ 5·10^8 ε^{-2}

quote_A.text: For every masa A⊆M⊆B(H) and every x=x*∈M, the element x is (ε,r_ε) so-pavable over A ... r_ε ≤ 500000000ε^{-2}

quote_B.text: resolving the Popa–Vaes quadratic paving conjecture

notes: Headline taken from summary (quadratic SO paving); existence of paving with explicit block count, M8 arguable. Companion manuscript proves the approximation-paving half of Popa–Vaes Conj. 2.8(1) with C ε^{-6} blocks.

claim_formal: ∀ Grothendieck coherator C (Ara–Henry convention): the homotopy theory of C-∞-groupoids is equivalent to that of spaces (via elementary expansions being weak equivalences)

quote_A.text: its weak globular infinity-groupoids recover the homotopy theory of spaces

quote_B.text: We prove the Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis for every Grothendieck coherator in the Ara–Henry convention ... We also resolve Henry's pushout conjecture

notes: Main theorem in the paper is Henry's pushout conjecture (elementary expansions are weak equivalences); the homotopy hypothesis follows via Henry's prior reduction (semi-model structure). Lean formalizes only the elementary-expansion theorem (intermediate result). Restriction to the Ara–Henry coherator convention could argue O5.

claim_formal: ∃ separable real Banach spaces X,Y ∃ bijection Ψ:X→Y: (4/21)‖s−t‖ ≤ ‖Ψs−Ψt‖ ≤ (76/25)‖s−t‖ ∧ X ≇ Y linearly

quote_A.text: There are separable real Banach spaces X,Y and a bijection Ψ:X→Y such that ... In particular, X and Y are not linearly isomorphic.

quote_B.text: This gives a negative answer to the separable Banach-space Lipschitz-isomorphism problem.

notes: Question asked by Aharoni–Lindenstrauss (1978); Kalton's survey lists it as Problem 3 (survey repeat → P2 by rule 8). Second manuscript: bi-Lipschitz absorption of c0 without a linear copy of c0.

claim_formal: ∀ n≥3 ∃ C_n ∀ complete connected (M^n,g) with −4Δ+Scal ≥ 1 ∃ continuous f:M→K, dim K ≤ n−2, ∀y: diam f^{-1}(y) ≤ C_n

quote_A.text: admits a continuous map f:M→K to a simplicial complex of dimension at most n−2 such that diam_g f^{-1}(y) ≤ C_n

quote_B.text: This extends the uniform Urysohn width theorem from a pointwise scalar-curvature lower bound to a spectral lower bound.

notes: Headline (summary lead) is the spectral generalization of the companion theorem in the same family proving Gromov's uniform codim-2 Urysohn width conjecture for Scal≥1 (which alone would be P1/O1). Corollaries: macroscopic dimension ≤ n−2 for universal covers of PSC manifolds, filling-radius bound, no PSC on closed aspherical n≥4 manifolds. n=3 has explicit constant 500/√λ.

claim_formal: ∀ closed connected Einstein 4-manifold (M,g) with Ric=λg, λ>0, sec≥0: universal cover ≅ (up to scale) round S^4, Fubini–Study CP^2, or S^2×S^2 with equal radii

quote_A.text: up to scaling, their universal Riemannian covers are the round S4, Fubini–Study CP2, or a product of equal round two-spheres

quote_B.text: The companion manuscript proves the strictly positive classification without additional curvature or topological restrictions.

notes: Positive-sectional-curvature Einstein 4-manifold classification is a long-standing folklore conjecture (could be P2). Lean formalizes only the strictly positive case (weaker). L2 topological gap theorem is conditional on a Classification Assumption.

claim_formal: ∀ closed connected Riemannian (M^n,g), n≥2, satisfying weak MTW, ∀ x∈M: tangent injectivity domain I(x) is convex

quote_A.text: If (M,g) satisfies weak MTW, then I(x) is convex for every x∈M.

quote_B.text: resolving Villani's conjecture in this setting

notes: 'in this setting' = compact boundaryless; paper says the conjecture in the compact setting imposes no nonfocality, so O1. Corollary: uniform bi-Hölder optimal transport maps (also in Lean).

claim_formal: ∀ bounded connected smooth Ω⊂ℝ^3, ∀ smooth (λ_j,μ_j) with μ_j>0, 3λ_j+2μ_j>0: Λ_{λ1,μ1}=Λ_{λ2,μ2} → (λ1,μ1)=(λ2,μ2)

quote_A.text: If Λ_{λ1,μ1}=Λ_{λ2,μ2} ... then λ1=λ2 and μ1=μ2 throughout Ω.

quote_B.text: This resolves the smooth three-dimensional isotropic elastic Calderón uniqueness problem under these positivity assumptions.

notes: Injectivity of the boundary map (M1; M4 arguable). Problem posed as the 3D elastic Calderón uniqueness question (2D done by Imanuvilov–Yamamoto); uniqueness expected, P1 arguable.
